name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_SyncToOwner
summary: Slot 1 of the field actor-action vtable: calls its own slot 12 (0x0036CE18, which returns -1, 2 or 3 from owner->f_2D4 and bit 3 of owner->f_2CC) and forwards that state code to the owner actor through the actor's vt[0x84]. The old doc said it asked the owner for a value; it asks itself.
evidence: Vtable 0x007656F0 slot 1, and that table's slot 3 is the confident Field_ActorAction_Update (0x0036D2E8) and slot 10 the confident Field_ActorAction_OnStateNotify (0x0036CC74), so the class is the field actor action. Disassembly of slot 12 (0x0036CE18: mvn r0,#0 / movne r0,#2 / movne r0,#3) shows the forwarded value is a small state code, not a pointer, so what the actor's vt[0x84] does with it is still open - kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_ActorTurnAction_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor (base vptr reset 0x00193E44, which writes the base vtable 0x00758AE0, then operator delete 0x0010F6CC) heading vtable 0x007656F0, the field actor-action table whose slot 3 is Field_ActorAction_Update and slot 10 Field_ActorAction_OnStateNotify. The 'ActorTurnAction' part of the name is unsupported.
evidence: Vtable 0x007656F0 slot 0; its slot 3 is the confident Field_ActorAction_Update (0x0036D2E8) and slot 10 the confident Field_ActorAction_OnStateNotify (0x0036CC74), so the class is the field actor action, not a turn action. The obvious name Field_ActorAction_DeletingDtor is already taken by 0x0036C304 (batch N_127, vtable 0x0076563C) whose body actually calls 0x001B7DB0, not 0x00193E44 - the two need reconciling before this one can drop maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_TurnAction_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor (base vptr reset 0x00193E44 + operator delete 0x0010F6CC) of a field action subclass whose vtable 0x00765730 adds an item-name formatter at slot 16 (0x0036D3AC: Item_LookupRecord on the u16 at self+0x12, then Text_FormatMessageArg) and Ui_ShowInfoMessage at slot 15, i.e. an action that shows an info message about an item. The 'TurnAction' label is still a guess.
evidence: Vtable 0x00765730 slot 0. New: its slot 16 is 0x0036D3AC, which resolves Item_LookupRecord(*(u16*)(self+0x12)) and formats it with Text_FormatMessageArg, and slot 15 is the confident Ui_ShowInfoMessage (0x002A4514); slot 14 (0x0036D3E8) is a second deleting destructor that unlinks self+8 from a list first. That pins the family (field action that reports an item) but not the class name, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_EpilogueTail
summary: Not a real entry point: 0x0036DCF6 is two bytes into the blt at 0x0036DCF4. The coherent code is the epilogue at 0x0036DCFC (ldr r0,[r4,#0xC]; add sp,sp,#0x480; pop {r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,pc}) of the action update that starts earlier.
evidence: Disassembly at 0x0036DCF4 is 'e2ffffba blt #0x36dc88', so the batch address lands inside that instruction; the readable C is a single halt_baddata. Nothing here is callable, so the name only labels a fragment.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_AttachTail
summary: Not a real entry point: 0x0036E566 is two bytes into the blt at 0x0036E564. The coherent code starts at 0x0036E56C (mov r0,r7; bl 0x0062F680; cmp r0,#0; beq ...), a fragment of the surrounding action-attach routine.
evidence: Disassembly at 0x0036E564 is '0c0000ba blt #0x36e5a0', so the batch address lands inside that instruction; the readable C is a single halt_baddata. The only named callee (maybe_Field2D_ApplyActorVisualState) belongs to the enclosing function, not to this address.

name: maybe_Field_ActorComponent_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor (base vptr reset 0x00193E44 + operator delete 0x0010F6CC) heading vtable 0x00765930, a field-actor component table whose slot 1 is the 1180-byte overlay-position routine 0x00371518 and slot 2 the interaction-state reset 0x003719B4.
evidence: Vtable 0x00765930 slot 0; the body is the standard vptr-reset + operator-delete pair. The class is only positional: both named siblings (maybe_Ui_Actor_CalcOverlayPosition, maybe_Field_Actor_ResetInteractionState) are themselves still maybe_, so 'Field_ActorComponent' cannot be confirmed.

name: maybe_Field_PlayerActor_ChangeMotionState
summary: Player-actor virtual (slot 12 of vtable 0x00765964) that applies the motion for the three-way mode byte at +0x74: mode 1 requests motion 0x17, mode -1 requests motion 3 (both through 0x005E7848) and both set +0x78 = 1. Mode 0 is handled by the two attachment slots 10/11 instead, so this slot only covers the non-zero modes.
evidence: Vtable 0x00765964 slot 12. New: slots 10 and 11 (0x00371E14 / 0x00371DDC) both gate on f_74 == 0, which shows +0x74 is a three-state mode and that this virtual is the non-zero-mode branch of the same switch. What modes 1 and -1 mean (sit / ride / swim) is still unknown, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_PlayerActor_SetAttachmentA
summary: Player-actor virtual (slot 11 of vtable 0x00765964): only in mode 0 of +0x74 it hands the 0x14-byte node at self+0x30 to the owner actor's vt[0x84], then clears the owner's selector byte +0x311. Its twin slot 10 (0x00371E14) does the same with the node at +0x44 and sets +0x311 = 1.
evidence: Vtable 0x00765964 slot 11, immediately after slot 10 (0x00371E14); the two bodies differ only in the node address (+0x30 vs +0x44) and the value written to owner+0x311 (0 vs 1), so they are a two-way attachment selector. What the nodes and the +0x311 flag mean is still unknown.

name: maybe_Field_PlayerActor_SetAttachmentB
summary: Twin of slot 11: in mode 0 of +0x74 it hands the 0x14-byte node at self+0x44 to the owner actor's vt[0x84] and sets the owner's selector byte +0x311 = 1.
evidence: Vtable 0x00765964 slot 10, adjacent to slot 11 (0x00371DDC); identical body except the node (+0x44) and the flag value (1). The pair is a two-way attachment selector, but the meaning of the nodes and of +0x311 is unverified.

name: Field_PlayerActor_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the player-controlled field actor: runs the class destructor 0x001E1B88 (which chains to the base object destructor 0x001E1B70) and frees the block with operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: Heads vtable 0x00765964, whose slot 1 is the confident Field_Actor_ResetStep (0x00371A28), slot 3 the confident Field_Actor_UpdateInputDirection (0x00371E4C) and slot 14 the confident Model_ApplyFacingTilt (0x00371A44), and whose slots 10-12 are the player-only attachment/motion virtuals. That pins the class to the player-controlled field actor, so the maybe_ prefix can go.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_CloseSlotB
summary: Sends state 4 to the object's vt[0x3C] and clears the byte at +0x9C. Its only caller is the field actor-interaction dispatcher 0x001CC6D8 (call site 0x001CC83C), so the 'Ui_Window' attribution is unverified.
evidence: No vtable in .rodata points at this address, and the single caller 0x001CC6D8 is a battle/field actor-interaction dispatcher (it reads battle work +0x4244, Game_GetDataManager and 0x0063E05C message rows), not a UI screen. The body is a plain 'send state 4 + clear a byte', so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_CloseSlotC
summary: Same shape as 0x003781E0 but clears the byte at +0x26E instead of +0x9C; called from the same field actor-interaction dispatcher 0x001CC6D8 (call site 0x001CC8CC).
evidence: No vtable points at this address; the only caller is 0x001CC6D8, the same dispatcher that calls 0x003781E0, and the two bodies differ only in the cleared offset (+0x9C vs +0x26E). The class is therefore still unknown.

name: maybe_Container_InvokeMemberIfReady
summary: Invokes a stored member-function pointer (this-adjustment encoded in bit 0 of the flags word at self[1]) when the callable test 0x00284D88 on arg2+0x24C succeeds, then bumps the counter at self[2] and resets it if the pointer changed. Both named callers are UI constructors, so this is a UI delegate/callback invoke rather than a container operation.
evidence: New: the callee 0x00284D88 is the same 'is this member pointer callable' test the body itself performs (returns 1 when [p+4] != 0 or ([p+8] & 1) != 0), and the two callers are Ui_PokerWindow_Ctor (0x001E3E78) and maybe_PartyPanel_CreateSlotObject (0x001E24B4). That makes it a delegate invoke with a re-entrancy counter; the 'Container' part of the name is unsupported.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_GetRowData
summary: Fills a 6-byte row descriptor: resolves the current slot through 0x006508B0(window+0x2B0), follows the self-relative u16 pointer at slot+4 into *out, sets out[1] = out[2] = 1 and maps the category byte at window+0x3DE8 (0 -> 2, 1 -> 1, 2 -> 0) into out[5]. Returns 0 when the slot pointer is null.
evidence: New: 0x006508B0 is a slot accessor (returns self+0x70 + u16([self+0x38]+0xC)*8), and the u16 it resolves is stored as an offset relative to its own address - a table-relative pointer, not a plain id. The only caller is maybe_Menu_ShowRowDescriptionPopup, so the class and the 'row data' wording remain guesses.

name: maybe_Ui_MemoriesWindow_HandleInputB
summary: Entry 0 of the memories-window handler table at 0x0072B7B4 (entries 1 and 2 are the confident Ui_MemoriesWindow_HandleInput and Ui_MemoriesWindow_UpdateScene). It runs the same f_20D8 input-bit tests as 0x0037ADB4 but without the unlock check: confirm applies the grid-cursor selection, cancel sets the state byte to 3 and selects state 4.
evidence: New: the address is the first {fn, 0} pair of the handler table at 0x0072B7B4, whose next pairs are Ui_MemoriesWindow_HandleInput (0x0037ADB4), Ui_MemoriesWindow_UpdateScene (0x0037AEAC) and 0x0037B224. That confirms the memories-window family and the input-handler role; the 'B' suffix is still arbitrary, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite_InvokeEventHandler
summary: Slot 29 of the Gfx sprite scene-node vtable 0x00764C6C (whose slot 1 is the confident Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance): gates on the global handler-registry entry at 0x0072840C selected by self->f_2A0, then calls self->f_29C(self->f_2A0, self->f_2A4, self) and returns 0.
evidence: New: the old doc's 'vtable 0x00764BB0 slot 29' was off by one table - 0x00361FC4 is slot 29 of the vtable that starts at 0x00764C6C (slot 0 = 0x00362080, slot 1 = Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance 0x005F2B54), so the sprite attribution holds. The disassembly shows the call goes through the object field +0x29C with the two fields +0x2A0/+0x2A4 as arguments, and the global table at 0x0072840C only gates it; what the handler is remains unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_DtorDelete
summary: Scalar deleting destructor that stores the vtable argument in the object, runs the shared window destructor 0x005F8528 (vptr reset plus release of the +0x1EC list) and frees with operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The body shape is certain (vtable store + 0x005F8528 + 0x0010F6CC), but no .rodata word points at this address, so it is not a vtable head, and the only caller 0x002183F4 (maybe_Ui_Window_ReleaseChildAndRequestMode) is itself unnamed. The 'GuideWindow' class is still purely positional (between 0x003A9834 and 0x003A98A4).

name: maybe_Ui_FourRowList_Reset
summary: Resets a four-row window: stores the text id at +0x28, formats the caption from 0x003F7274 into pane 7, clears the row-slot byte +0x49 and the four per-row bytes at +0x13 (stride 5), sets every row's pane to the empty value and finishes by calling its own vt[0x18](self, 1).
evidence: The confirmed sibling 0x003F1AF0 (Ui_FourRowIconWindow_InitPanes) uses the same +0x49 row-slot byte and the same txt_l1 / null_txt_l1 pane naming, which supports the four-row window family; the class of 0x003F71C0 itself and the 'Reset' wording are still guesses because its callers 0x003F6F20 / 0x003F7290 are unnamed.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_ActionSequence_MarkSlots
summary: Not a real entry point: it is the continuation of 0x003C36E8 after the beq at 0x003C36FC, and the readable C is a single bogus CONCAT44 on unaff_r9. The block marks byte +0x108 on each of the N widgets returned by the widget's vt[0x48].
evidence: Disassembly shows 0x003C36E8 falls through into 0x003C3704 (mov r0,r4 at 0x003C3700, then bl 0x00630DC8 at 0x003C3704), so this address is mid-function; the C body is destroyed (unaff_r9, CONCAT44). The slot-marking reading comes only from the disassembly (strb r8,[r0,#0x108] inside the loop).

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_Update
summary: Slot 0 of the four Battle_Ui_MemberWidget vtables: fetches the sequence object at self+0x122C, asks 0x00630DC8 for the pending count, marks byte +0x108 on each widget returned by vt[0x48], then handles the current widget's state 0x99 (including a vt[0xE8]/vt[0x128] probe).
evidence: New: the address is slot 0 of vtables 0x00763464, 0x00763938, 0x007694A0 and 0x00769C60, all of which have the confident Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_SelectActor (0x003C332C) at slot 1 - so the class is the battle member widget, not an 'ActionSequence'. The body is damaged (halt_baddata after the first branch), so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PlayPopupSe
summary: Shared tail block (no frame of its own) that plays SE 0x15E (350) at volume 1.0 through Sound_GetPlayer + Sound_PlaySeById; reached by tail-branch from three Battle_ActionSequence processors (ExecuteMemberActions, ProcessDefaultAction, ProcessState5). The 'popup' attribution is unverified.
evidence: New: the named callees settle what it does - 0x006F1DF8 is Sound_GetPlayer and 0x001EBC68 Sound_PlaySeById, and the literal pool gives r1 = 0x15E, s0 = 1.0f, s1 = 0.0f, so it is a SE play and not the fade the first pass guessed. The three callers are all action-sequence processors, so 'popup' is still a guess about which SE 350 is.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PushMessageIfStateFlag
summary: Tail-merged block that reads the battle-work 3D/2D flag at work+0x4244 (Os_GetGameWork -> +8 -> +0x5C) and, only when it is set, queues a battle message with the pending message id kept in r7.
evidence: The readable C is destroyed (returns in_r12 + arg1), so the whole reading comes from the disassembly. The work offsets (+8 -> +0x5C -> +0x4244) match the established battle-work layout, but the 'message' wording rests on a single mov r1,#0xF, and there is still no caller.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_SetSequenceEndFlag
summary: Tail-merged block of the action-sequence updater: calls the bag routine 0x006138D4 with id 3 (Game_GetWork -> +0x24A98) and then sets the 'sequence finished' byte at self+0xF1C to 1 if it was still 0.
evidence: The readable C is halt_baddata. The named globals in the disassembly (Game_GetWork, bag at +0x24A98) show the call goes to the bag/storage object rather than to a UI core as the first pass said, but what 0x006138D4 does with id 3 is unknown and there is no caller.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_ApplyCommand
summary: Body of the member-widget virtual that starts at 0x003C6BE0 (slot 9 of vtable 0x00763464; 0x003C6BE4 is the continuation after the add r1,r0,#0x1000 prologue). It dispatches on unit->f_260->f_29D: mode 3 asks the UI for the action record (ui->vt[0x40]) and forwards (1, record, message id) to unit->f_22C->vt[0x4C]; modes 1 and 2 only call vt[0x50] with 1.
evidence: New: the vtable slot at 0x00763488 points at 0x003C6BE0, and 0x003C6BE4 is four bytes later, so this address is the body of a member-widget virtual rather than a free function. Two 'could not recover jumptable' warnings and the indirect calls through unit+0x22C keep the decompilation unreliable, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchByUnit
signature: void maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchByUnit(void* seq, u32 forwarded, void* cmd)
summary: When the command object reports idle (cmd->vt[0x10] == 0) it looks up a per-unit byte in the 0x68-stride table at seq+0xBAFE+seq[0x3780]*0x68 and calls 0x0039881C(seq+0x164, seq->vt[0x48](seq,0), cmd, forwarded, entry) - with entry 0 when the table byte is 0, or only when cmd->vt[0x24] accepts.
evidence: No caller, and the dispatch target 0x0039881C is still unnamed, so what the call starts stays opaque. The table stride and the two virtual probes are read straight from the code; the 'Battle' attribution rests only on the neighbouring action-sequence functions.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionAnimObject_SetFinished
summary: Sixteen-byte stub that calls 0x001F43D4 and returns 1, the 'handled' value the surrounding event handlers use when they finish an action animation.
evidence: It is the first word of the table at 0x00769658, but that table's other entries are UI widget methods (0x001F4434, 0x00630CDC Container_FindObjectByTypeIdJ, 0x001F909C), so the 'ActionAnimObject' class attribution is unverified; 0x001F43D4 is not an entry point in the merged table either.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionAnimObject_DtorDeleteB
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: base destructor 0x00322D14 (a tail branch to the vptr reset 0x00193E44) followed by operator delete 0x0010F6CC. It heads vtable 0x00769754, whose slot 1 requests a motion through the owner's vt[0x74] and whose slot 3 is a long update.
evidence: New: it is the first word of vtable 0x00769754, and that table's slot 1 (0x003CE0B8) calls owner->vt[0x74](owner, 3, 0, s0, s1) while slot 3 (0x003CE0E4) is a long update gated on 0x00669DD4 - so the class is an action object with a motion request. The 'ActionAnimObject' label is still inherited from the family grouping.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionAnimObject_DtorDeleteC
summary: Same two-call deleting destructor as 0x003CE2E4 (base destructor 0x00322D14 + operator delete 0x0010F6CC), heading vtable 0x00769788 whose slot 1 (0x002F09A8) requests motion 0 through 0x005E7848.
evidence: New: it is the first word of vtable 0x00769788, whose slot 1 is 0x002F09A8 (calls 0x005E7848(owner, 0, 0)) and whose slots 2/3 are empty stubs - so it is a sibling class of 0x003CE2E4 with the same base destructor. The raw function is 0xBC bytes but Ghidra kept only the two calls, so inlined member releases are missing from the readable C.

name: maybe_Battle_TargetMarker_DtorDelete
summary: Scalar deleting destructor (vptr reset 0x00193E44 + operator delete 0x0010F6CC) heading vtable 0x00769820, whose slots 1 and 3 are the update methods 0x003CFE5C and 0x003CFFA8.
evidence: New: it is the first word of vtable 0x00769820; slot 1 (0x003CFE5C) reads owner->f_273 and owner->f_160, and slot 3 (0x003CFFA8) is a state machine on self+0x64. That confirms an action-object class but not the 'TargetMarker' label, which is still inherited.

name: maybe_Menu_DrainPendingList
summary: Walks the intrusive list (head sentinel at +0, resume node at +0xC) and invokes each node's member-function pointer at node+0x1A4; when a node reports busy it remembers the next node and stops, and it sets the done byte +0x6A once the list is empty or a node stays busy.
evidence: The body is a plain intrusive-list walk with a done byte, and all seven callers are still unnamed screen-close / SE helpers (maybe_Ui_CloseScreenIfFlag, maybe_Menu_PlaySelectSe, ...), so only the 'drain pending list' wording is supported - the 'Menu' subsystem is a guess.

name: maybe_PendingList_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the intrusive list that 0x003D1454 drains: makes the three head words at +0..+8 point at the object, clears the bookkeeping, copies the two sentinel counters from 0x003D15BC/0x003D15C0 into +0x6C/+0x88/+0x8C and zeroes the 0x59-byte node array at +0x10.
evidence: New: the fields match the drainer exactly - this ctor sets the done byte +0x6A to 0 and the resume node +0xC to 0, which are precisely the two fields 0x003D1454 reads and writes. That drainer is called only from UI screen-close / SE helpers, so the old 'Gfx_ResourceHandleList' subsystem was wrong; the list itself is a pending-work list, hence the vaguer name.

name: maybe_Ui_AmountSpinner_DtorDelete
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: class destructor 0x001D8C2C (vptr reset plus unlink of the +0x114 list) followed by operator delete 0x0010F6CC. It heads vtable 0x00769AA8, whose slots 4-6 are the range-check / update methods 0x003D273C, 0x003D2810 and 0x003D27CC.
evidence: New: it is the first word of vtable 0x00769AA8, whose slot 4 (0x003D273C) does a range check on self+0x11C and whose slots 5/6 are the paired update methods - so the deleting-destructor role is solid. The 'AmountSpinner' class name still comes only from the neighbouring resolver stubs.

name: Ui_EquipWindow_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the equipment window: runs the shared window destructor 0x005F8528 (vptr reset plus release of the +0x1EC list) and frees with operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: Heads vtable 0x00769F58, whose slot 1 is the confident Ui_EquipWindow_Init (0x003D4834) and whose remaining slots are the Gfx node methods (0x005F7F30, 0x005F6C14, 0x005F6018 ...), so the class is the equipment window and the maybe_ prefix can go. Spelled DeletingDtor rather than DtorDelete because 0x0046CFB4 already carries Ui_EquipWindow_DtorDelete (batch N_111) and merge_names rejects duplicate names.

name: maybe_Ui_DungeonHpWindow_HidePane
summary: Calls the element flag setter 0x0029126C on the element at self+0x138 with 0. The setter stores the byte at element+0x14 and mirrors bit 0 into the element user's +0x44, so this is a plain two-argument flag write; whether 0 means hidden is still unknown.
evidence: New: reading 0x0029126C in the disassembly shows the exact flag semantics (byte at +0x14, bit 0 mirrored into user+0x44), which explains why Ghidra reports the call as non-returning - the tail call lost its frame. The polarity and the 'DungeonHpWindow' class are still unverified; the only caller is maybe_Menu_UpdateResultWindow.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoTextWindow_DtorDelete
signature: void maybe_Ui_TwoTextWindow_DtorDelete(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Deleting destructor of a multiply-inherited window: rewrites five interface vtable pointers inside the object (+0x00, 0x134, 0x168, 0x1A0, 0x224), stores the argument at +0x224, then runs the class destructor 0x001D8C2C and frees with 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The five simultaneous vtable stores only prove 'a class with five base sub-objects'. New: the +0x224 word it stores is the same mode byte that 0x003D59B4 writes, so the two belong to one class; the 'TwoTextWindow' label still rests only on the neighbouring maybe_Ui_TwoTextWindow_Ctor (0x003D59F8).

name: maybe_Ui_DungeonOperationWindow_SetMode
summary: Selects the window's mode: resolves text id 0x23 (0x24 when mode is 0) through 0x00213E30 / 0x006406D0, writes it into pane 1 of the pane at +0x138 and stores the mode byte at +0x224 - the same field the deleting destructor 0x003D5888 rewrites.

name: maybe_Ui_DungeonWindow_AnimCommand
summary: Sends animation command 0 to the controller at self+0x2C and runs it when the controller accepts (virtual +0x14 query, then virtual +0x10 run). It is slot 0 of the table at 0x0076A120, whose slots 1 and 2 are 0x003D5CC0 and 0x003D5C10, so the three share one controller protocol.
evidence: New: the address is slot 0 of the table at 0x0076A120 (slot 1 = 0x003D5CC0, slot 2 = 0x003D5C10, then the shared base slots 0x00193C6C / 0x00193CD8 / 0x00193CD4 / 0x0062A704 ...), so the three are one class's controller commands. The class itself and the 'DungeonWindow' label are still unverified.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_FindOrAddSlot
summary: Gated on the actor model being ready (0x00669DD4): scans the two-word slot table at self+0x2C for an entry equal to 1 and returns 1 if found, otherwise appends a new entry set to 1 and increments the count at +0x48. It returns 1 on every path, so callers can only be using the side effect.
evidence: The full body is visible and shows the unconditional return 1, which contradicts a predicate framing - the name describes the side effect (find-or-append a slot), not a return value. No caller is named, so what the slot = 1 sentinel means stays open.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_StopAnimAndPause
summary: Stops the actor's current motion through the model virtual +0x88 and then sends animation command 2 to the controller at +0x2C, running it if the controller accepts. Slot 1 of the table at 0x0076A120.
evidence: New: it is slot 1 of the same table as 0x003D5AE8 (0x0076A120), so both use the controller protocol at self+0x2C. The 'Pause' half of the name is invented - the code only sends command 2 - and the class is still unverified, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_SubWidget_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor (shared window destructor 0x005F8528 + operator delete 0x0010F6CC) heading vtable 0x0076A154, whose slot 1 is the config-init 0x003D5E58 and slot 2 the confident Gfx_Node_Dtor (0x005F7F98).
evidence: New: it is the first word of vtable 0x0076A154, which continues with 0x003D5E58 (allocates a 0xEC-byte block after 0x005F541C) and the confident Gfx_Node_Dtor 0x005F7F98 - so it is a Gfx-node-derived UI sub-widget, not a 'Field_ActorUi' as the first pass said. The sub-widget's identity is still only the config-init neighbour.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ResetState
summary: Resets the message window's page state: clears +0x3778/+0x3779, marks the embedded page record at +0x37D4 dirty, sets +0x3778 again when the page's text field reports content (0x0018CC14) and finally pushes the page text through 0x00100B74.
evidence: New: the address is slot 4 of the message-window vtable 0x0076A46C (slot 0 = 0x003D717C, slot 1/2 = 0x0029FA00/0x0029F9F4), which supports the message-window attribution. The callee 0x0018CC14 is now named Text_ResolveStyleBlock, so the 'has content' reading is plausible but the class is still only from the vtable family.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_DispatchPageCallback
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_DispatchPageCallback(void* self, u32 unchanged, int current)
summary: Message-window page bookkeeping: marks the page layer dirty when the current page is not one of the default ones, then dispatches the current page's callback from the 12-byte page table at +0x134 (function pointer plus flags, with the usual odd-flag member-pointer form).
evidence: New: the address is slot 0 of the message-window vtable 0x0076A46C, whose slot 4 is 0x003D70E0 - so both are message-window methods. The page table layout is read from the code, but the callback target is unrecovered and the class is only from the vtable family.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_UpdateSelectionVisualB
summary: Entry 0 of the dive-form handler table at 0x0072C538: when bit 2 of +0x3770 is set it only refreshes the command list at +0x134 through 0x006D89DC, otherwise it runs the 532-byte selection update. Its twin 0x003D8184 (entry 0 of the table at 0x0072C508) has the same prologue.
evidence: New: the address is the first {fn, 0} pair of the handler table at 0x0072C538 (0x003D7BC8, 0x002CF8C0, 0x003D82E0, 0x003D7EAC, 0x003D7F6C, 0x003D73D4), and 0x003D8184 is the first pair of the parallel table at 0x0072C508 - so both are dive-form state handlers. The 'B' suffix and the 'SelectionVisual' wording are still guesses.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_SetPaneFlag
summary: Sets the element at self+0x2A4 through the element flag setter 0x0029126C, passing the inverse of the requested state (the setter stores the byte at element+0x14 and mirrors bit 0 into the element user's +0x44), then continues with the +0x400 pane.
evidence: New: reading 0x0029126C in the disassembly shows the exact flag semantics (byte at +0x14, bit 0 mirrored into user+0x44), which explains the on == 0 inversion in the call. Which polarity means 'visible' is still unknown, and the class is only from the caller Ui_MultiTextWindow_Ctor.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_UpdateSelectionVisual
summary: Entry 0 of the dive-form handler table at 0x0072C508: with bit 2 of +0x3770 set it only refreshes the command list at +0x134 (0x006D89DC), otherwise it applies the current entry's three signed angle bytes to the model at +0x388, marks +0x3778 and the render object visible and continues at 0x003D6C18.
evidence: New: the address is the first {fn, 0} pair of the handler table at 0x0072C508 (0x003D8184, 0x003D84DC, 0x002B1A9C, 0x003D800C, 0x003D7240, 0x003D837C), which confirms the dive-form family. The readable body is two halt_baddata stubs, so the whole reading comes from the disassembly and the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_ApplyValueStep
summary: Value-step handler: copies the chosen record's widget state (record+0x35C) into self+0x210 through Ui_Widget_Update, then polls 0x0062F680 on self+0x210 and, when the cursor animation has finished, plays SE 2 and hides the form through 0x003D85D8(self, 0).
evidence: The readable C is destroyed (a bogus call to func_0x00f51e9e plus halt_baddata), so the reading comes from the disassembly: add r1,r1,#0x35C / add r0,r0,#0x210 / bl 0x001DAD58 (Ui_Widget_Update), then bl 0x0062F680 and mov r0,#2. The neighbours maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnValueStep (0x003D82E0) and Ui_DiveForm_SetVisible (0x003D85D8) keep it plausible but unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotTable_NextIndex
signature: void maybe_Ui_SlotTable_NextIndex(void* self, u8* out, u32 mode)
summary: Advances the slot table's cursor: when the byte count at +0x23C is set it copies that many bytes out, otherwise it increments the counter at +0x234 (capped by +0x238) and byte-swaps it. The rest of the body is unrecoverable coprocessor/pseudo instructions.
evidence: New: no RNG call appears anywhere in the body or in the disassembly prologue (ldrb r0,[r0,#0x23C] / ldm r0,{r0,r1} on +0x234), so the 'Random' part of the old name was unsupported and has been dropped. The body still contains coprocessor_load / in_cr8 / unaff_r10 and ends in halt_baddata, so the name keeps maybe_ at low confidence.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_DtorDeleteB
summary: Deleting destructor: class destructor 0x0028EFB4 (stores two vtable pointers for the multiply-inherited object, then calls 0x004AF56C) followed by operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: New: it is the first word of vtable 0x0076A744, whose slots 2 and 4 are 0x0028EE3C and 0x003DDA70 and whose remaining slots are Gfx-node methods (0x005F8120, 0x005F6C14, 0x005F6018 ...) - so the class is a Gfx-node / Actor2D-derived object, not a plain field actor. The 'Field_Actor' label is therefore unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ClearPaneFlag
summary: First calls the element flag setter 0x0029126C with the incoming arguments, then reads the UI core through 0x006F229C and drives the +0x1C sub-object. Ghidra lost the register arguments of the setter call, so the target element is only known to be one of the window's panes.
evidence: New: the disassembly shows the body is longer than the readable C - after the 0x0029126C call it does mov r0,sp / bl 0x006F229C (Ui_GetCore) and then walks [core+0x14]+0x1C. The 'ClearPaneFlag' reading therefore covers only the first block, and the class is still only from the neighbouring 0x003DE600 / 0x003DEA44 pair.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ResetPageFlag
summary: 508-byte message-window routine whose readable C keeps only the head: when the page counter at +0x8A8 is 0 it clears the text-pane flag at +0x138 through 0x0029126C. The bulk of the body (the +0x8A8 != 0 branch at 0x003DEC2C) is missing from the C.
evidence: New: the disassembly shows ldr r0,[r0,#0x8A8] / cmp r0,#0 / bne 0x003DEC2C, so the readable C only covers the == 0 path and the 'ResetPageFlag' wording describes just that first block. The +0x8A8 page counter is the same field maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateAnim advances, which supports the end-of-page reading.
